title: MRI Study of OnabotulinumtoxinA (OnabotA) Effect on Jaw Muscle Pain
official: MRI-based Comparison of OnabotulinumtoxinA (OnabotA) Versus Placebo Injections to the Temporalis and Masseter Muscles in the Management of Myofascial Pain Syndrome: A Randomized Clinical Trial
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn which magnetic resonance images are best able to assess and predict if a participant with masticatory myofascial pain syndrome will benefit from Botox injections, as compared to placebo (saline, salt water).

The main questions the study aims to answer are:

* Will diffusion MR images will be best able to assess and predict if a participant with masticatory myofascial pain syndrome will benefit from Botox injections?
* Will Botox injections reduce masticatory myofascial pain and improve jaw function?
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Participant is at least 18 years of age
* Participant has a unilateral or bilateral myofascial pain diagnosis according to the Diagnostic Criteria for Temporomandibular Disorders (DC/TMD), diagnosed by a provider

Exclusion Criteria:

* Participant is pregnant, breastfeeding, or plans to become pregnant
* Participant has known hypersensitivity to any botulinum toxin preparation or to any of the components in the formulation
* Participant has received Botox within the past 4 months
* Participant cannot undergo an MRI. Reasons a participant cannot undergo MRIs for this study include having a pacemaker or having claustrophobia
* Participant has dental implants with metal on the same side/sides of their jaw pain
sponsor: Weill Medical College of Cornell University
